title: expr

arguments.description: expression including operators, functions, inlet types, float and symbols

body:
[expr] evaluates C-like expressions at control rate. Inlets are defined by variables of the form $t#, where 't' is the type and # is the inlet number, counting from 1 at the left (up to 100): $f# is a float, $i# is an integer (floats are truncated) and $s# is a symbol, used for array names. Text in quotes is a symbol string, and [expr] can also output symbols.

Multiple expressions separated by semicolons (up to 100) create one outlet each. They are evaluated from right to left, so the rightmost outlet fires first.

Arrays and variables (defined with [value]) are accessed as in C: "tab[5]" is element 5 of the array "tab", "$s2[5]" is element 5 of the array whose name came into inlet 2, and "valx + 10" adds 10 to the [value] named "valx". The store function "=" writes the result of an operation into a variable or array index, as in "tab[$f1] = $f2".

Besides the C operators (arithmetic, relational, bitwise and logical), the available functions are:
math: min, max, int, rint, round, trunc, nearbyint, float, abs, fmod, remainder, floor, ceil, modf, imodf, copysign, ldexp, hypot, if, random, isnan, isinf, finite
power and log: pow, sqrt, cbrt, exp, expm1, ln, log, log10, log1p, fact, erf, erfc
trigonometry: sin, cos, tan, asin, acos, atan, atan2, sinh, cosh, tanh, asinh, acosh, atanh
tables: size, sum, Sum, avg, Avg
acoustics: mtof, ftom, dbtorms, rmstodb, dbtopow, powtodb
symbols and strings: symbol, sym, var, strlen, strcat, strncat, strcmp, strncmp, strcasecmp, strncasecmp, strpbrk, strspn, strcspn, tolower, tonlower, toupper, tonupper
